How to Resolve an IT Ticket

Responsible Teams and Roles
IT Help Desk, IT Security, System Administrators

IT Ticket Resolution Runbook

Purpose
This runbook explains how IT support should triage, investigate, resolve, and close internal technology tickets. It applies to access issues, device problems, software failures, shared inbox outages, VPN problems, and general business-system support.

When to Use
Use this runbook for all internal IT requests unless a specialist security incident or major outage process takes precedence.

Responsible Roles
Primary owner: IT Help Desk analyst.
Escalation owners: System Administrator, Network Engineer, or IT Security depending on issue type.
Approver: IT Manager when privileged access or emergency changes are involved.

Procedure
Step 1: Review the ticket summary, impacted user or team, urgency, and business impact.
Step 2: Confirm the request category such as access issue, device issue, application issue, mailbox issue, or connectivity issue.
Step 3: Collect minimum diagnostic data including screenshots, timestamps, device name, account name, and recent changes.
Step 4: Check whether the issue matches a known problem, outage notice, or recent change record.
Step 5: Attempt standard troubleshooting steps appropriate to the category, such as credential reset, permission refresh, device restart, or configuration validation.
Step 6: If the issue involves privileged access, suspicious activity, or sensitive data exposure, pause standard handling and route to IT Security.
Step 7: If the ticket cannot be resolved at first line, escalate with a concise technical summary and all evidence gathered.
Step 8: Once a fix is applied, validate with the user that the issue is resolved and note the exact action taken.
Step 9: Update the ticket with resolution details, root cause if known, and any preventive follow-up.
Step 10: Close the ticket only after user confirmation or documented verification of restored service.

Approval Requirements
Privileged access changes require data-owner or manager approval.
Emergency production-impacting changes require IT Manager approval and post-change documentation.
Security-related tickets may require Compliance or Security review depending on scope.

Completion Criteria
The ticket is complete when service is restored, the action is documented, and any required follow-up or problem-management item has been logged.
